what_happened: The operator ran the parallel-jobs build (job q0xy) directly, ahead of the order in Athena's plan. The plan put the owner's speed priority last because every rung defaulted to the same kind of work. The operator overrode the plan's order and filed gap k0w6. This is the second time in a day the operator had to run the owner's top-priority speed work out of order.
cause: Planning does not take the owner's stated priority as an input. Rungs default to one work type and are sequenced by that default. Nothing compares the plan's order with the owner's latest priority. The queue also has no priority support, so the only way to change order is for the operator to bypass the plan. The earlier case (crny) logged gap k0w6's problem, but it was not fixed, so it happened again on the next speed job.
prevention: Make the owner's priorities, recorded from requests and addenda, a required input to plan ordering. Give each plan rung a rank derived from them. Add a code check that fails plan creation, or flags the plan, when the rung order contradicts the latest stated priority or when all rungs carry the default type with no ranking. Make the queue and drain honor the rank, so the plan's order is the run order and no operator bypass is needed.
proposed_request: Make Athena's plan order work by the owner's stated priority instead of by default rung type. Outcome: when the owner's addenda name a top priority (such as speed), the plan puts the jobs serving it first, and the queue runs them in that order, with no operator bypass. Acceptance: (1) the plan records the owner's current priorities and a rank for each rung; (2) plan creation fails or flags when the rung order contradicts the latest stated priority, or when every rung has the default type and no rank; (3) the queue drain runs by rank, and ties go oldest first; (4) a test shows that, given a speed-first addendum, the parallel-jobs build and the CI-routing build are sequenced ahead of the other rungs. This closes gap k0w6.
